sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's accelerating digital payments adoption, supported by regulatory push and expanding e-commerce, creates a sustained revenue base for fintech and software-as-a-service providers.
The government's 'Making Indonesia 4.0' roadmap and increased tech infrastructure spending drive long-term demand for enterprise solutions, cloud services, and cybersecurity.
Rising domestic venture capital and private equity activity in Indonesian tech startups fuels M&A and IPO pipelines, offering premium growth opportunities for listed tech firms.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's tech sector outperformed regionally (+0.44% vs -0.02% agg), driven by strong earnings and AI tailwinds. Key movers like MCAS (+19.55%) and SHOP (+11.54%) signal robust demand for enterprise software and digital payments. Maintain overweight on select names with local market penetration, as structural digitization and rising middle-class consumption provide durable growth catalysts.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's downstream processing mandate for nickel and bauxite continues to drive value-add and protect local miners from commodity price volatility.
Coal demand remains resilient due to domestic power plant needs and China/India import reliance, despite global decarbonization pressures.
Rising infrastructure spending and EV battery supply chain integration create durable demand for energy and mineral extraction in Indonesia.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's mining & energy sector shows strong local momentum (+1.43%) despite US weakness, with small-cap movers like ALKA and BAJA surging over 24%. Focus on domestic demand drivers—coal and nickel remain structural plays amid global supply constraints and Indonesia's downstream push.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's mandatory biodiesel blending (B35) and upcoming B40 mandate create durable demand for palm oil-based renewables, benefiting domestic producers like MPOW and BRPT.
US solar inverter and module makers (ENPH, SEDG, FSLR) face structural margin compression from Chinese oversupply and high US interest rates, favoring Indonesian manufacturing cost advantages.
Indonesia's nickel downstreaming policy for EV batteries and solar panel supply chains positions local climate-tech firms to capture global energy transition capex flows away from China.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables sector shows relative strength (+0.63%) versus US peers (-0.87%), driven by MPOW's +6.93% surge likely on domestic policy catalysts. Focus on local champions like BRPT (+1.45%) as Indonesia's energy transition accelerates under new government mandates, while US solar names (ENPH, ARRY) face headwinds from rate sensitivity.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rising middle-class consumption and urbanization sustain demand for branded packaged foods and beverages, driving volume growth for companies like AISA and AGAR.
Government focus on food security and downstream processing supports local FMCG players, reducing import dependence and boosting margins.
Digitalization and e-commerce penetration in lower-tier cities expand distribution reach for consumer goods, benefiting agile companies like ZONE and NASI.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's consumer sector shows selective momentum, led by food and beverage names (AISA, AGAR) and niche players (KOBX, ZONE) on resilient domestic demand and post-election policy clarity. Watch for margin expansion in staple companies and potential M&A catalysts.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's e-commerce boom drives structural demand for last-mile and cold-chain logistics, insulating domestic players from global trade slowdowns.
Government infrastructure spending and downstreaming policies create durable tailwinds for port and bulk shipping operators like BLTA and RIGS.
US logistics weakness (-2.09%) highlights divergence; Indonesian logistics stocks benefit from local consumption and resource exports, not global trade cycles.
sectors.ai: Logistics sector flat, but Indonesian names show selective strength. SDMU surged 6.49% on domestic volume optimism, while BLTA and TMAS gained on steady shipping demand. Avoid US-exposed names; focus on Indonesia's resilient e-commerce and commodity haulage plays for near-term alpha.

Global media consolidation and programmatic ad growth, evidenced by TTD and OMC, are creating spillover opportunities for Indonesian firms through cross-border partnerships.

Focus on RANS as a proxy for local digital monetization and MAPB for retail-media convergence, while US names like CHTR and TTD indicate global ad spend resilience.

Global DeFi and tokenization trends, particularly in real-world assets, are creating durable demand for blockchain infrastructure that Indonesia's resource-rich economy can leverage.
